expectations.text: Flags the nested comments and attachments resolvers as unscoped by tenant
expectations.evidence: Document.comments, attachments, and author are scoped by parent.id only... but the moment any other resolver returns a Document shape, the children are free

expectations.text: Flags updateDocument for scoping on id alone without a tenant constraint
expectations.evidence: where: { id: documentId } has no tenantId. Tenant A can overwrite the title/body of any document whose id it knows

expectations.text: Flags exportWorkspace taking tenantId from the client-controlled request body
expectations.evidence: tenantId comes from req.body, not the session... tenant_id in a request body is client-controlled, full stop

expectations.text: Flags searchDocuments as returning rows across all tenants
expectations.evidence: session is accepted and never used. Full-text search runs across every tenant's documents and returns ids and titles

expectations.text: Flags adminListDocuments as checking authentication but not authorization or tenant
expectations.evidence: The only check is "has a userId". Returns the 200 most recent documents across all tenants to any logged-in caller. There's no role check and no tenant scope

expectations.text: Enumerates all the affected sites rather than fixing only the first one found
expectations.evidence: Lists 5 findings ranked: exportWorkspace, updateDocument, searchDocuments, adminListDocuments, nested resolvers

expectations.text: Recommends a structural device (scoped repository, row-level security, or equivalent) rather than only adding where-clauses site by site
expectations.evidence: Postgres RLS... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY... A TenantDb built from the session (constructor requires tenantId), with the raw db lint-banned... Delete exportWorkspace's body-sourced tenant

expectations.text: Recommends a cross-tenant test that attempts tenant A operations against tenant B resources
expectations.evidence: The two-tenant test: create tenants A and B, call every exported function from A against B's ids, assert 404/empty

expectations.text: Identifies the raw interpolation of tenantId into $queryRawUnsafe as an injection hazard distinct in kind from the tenant-scoping bug
expectations.evidence: The id is also string-interpolated into $queryRawUnsafe, so ' OR 1=1 -- dumps the whole table. This one is a breach on its own

expectations.text: Does not conclude the main query paths being scoped means the service is safe
expectations.evidence: The "main query paths are scoped" claim is true — and that's exactly the pattern: getDocument and Query.documents are fine, everything off the happy path leaks
